title: pointcloud.org dataset manifest
description: Canonical schema for manifests/<...>/<id>/manifest.yaml -- schema_version 2, a rewrite (2026-08) that aligns the manifest's own field vocabulary directly with STAC (a Collection, plus per-item STAC-Item-shaped entries), instead of a bespoke vocabulary that merely got reflected into STAC output at ingest time. The manifest IS meant to read as a (partial) STAC Collection: only pointcloud.org-ingest-specific concerns that have no STAC equivalent (derivatives, federate, viewer settings, ...) are pulled out into the nested pointcloud_org object, so a reader who already knows STAC can read most of this file without a legend. scripts/validate-manifests.mjs validates every manifest against this file (via ajv) in CI, plus a few checks this file can't express on its own (see that script). pointcloud.org's ingest backend mirrors this same shape internally, except for the handful of fields resolved away before a manifest reaches it -- see this schema's own descriptions on those fields. See README.md for a walkthrough of adding a new dataset.

schema_version.description: Manifest schema version. Bumped from 1 (2026-08) when the manifest's vocabulary was rewritten to align with STAC -- see this schema's own top-level description.

type.description: Literal STAC type marker, same as a real STAC Collection document's own `type` field -- this manifest models one dataset as a Collection (its `items`/`items_dir`/`stac_item`/`external_source` entries become that Collection's child Items at ingest time).

stac_version.description: The STAC version this manifest's own vocabulary aligns to -- independent of whatever stac_version an externally-referenced stac_item happens to declare.

id.description: Dataset id -- must match this manifest's own directory name (the last path segment of manifests/.../<id>/), and must be globally unique across every manifest in this repo, regardless of how deeply nested it is. See "Grouping datasets into directories" in README.md.

description.description: STAC Collection's own `description` field -- "detailed multi-line description to fully explain the collection" per the spec. May contain Markdown -- rendered as sanitized HTML on the site. Plain text is valid Markdown too. May also be a bare relative filename ending in ".md" (e.g. "description.md") pointing at a Markdown file checked into this manifest's own directory alongside manifest.yaml -- use the file form for anything longer than a paragraph or two. The site's dataset-listing card view derives its short excerpt from this field's first line/paragraph -- there is deliberately no separate one-line "summary" field anymore (schema_version 1 had one; real STAC Collections don't).

id.description: The same SPDX identifier / Open Data Commons name this field would otherwise be, e.g. "CC-BY-4.0" or "Public Domain (U.S. Government Work)".

url.description: A URL to the actual terms-of-use page for this license, when the bare id alone doesn't point anywhere specific enough -- e.g. USGS-sourced data, whose "public domain" status is qualified by USGS's own usage FAQ rather than a single canonical SPDX/ODC license text.

license.description: STAC Collection's own `license` field is a plain SPDX/ODC string (or "various"/"proprietary") -- that plain-string form is the common case here too. The {id, url} object form is pointcloud.org's own convenience extension for a license that needs an accompanying terms-of-use link (e.g. USGS-sourced data): `id` becomes the real STAC `license` string, `url` (if given) becomes a `rel: "license"` Link -- the standard STAC way to attach one, so the generated Collection is still spec-plain either way.

keywords.description: STAC Collection common-metadata `keywords` field (renamed from schema_version 1's `tags`).

providers.description: STAC Collection provider objects -- flat {name, description, roles, url}, not schema_version 1's nested {organization: {name}}. At least one entry must carry a pointcloud_org.contact (used for ingest-failure notification emails) -- enforced here via 'contains'.

extent.description: STAC Collection's own `extent` object -- only `temporal` is manifest-authored (when the data's acquisition date/range is known); `spatial` is always computed from the ingested data itself at assembly time, never hand-authored here. `interval` follows the STAC convention exactly: an array of [start, end] pairs, either bound an ISO 8601 date/timestamp, `null` for open-ended.

sci:doi.description: STAC Scientific Citation extension. The dataset's own DOI, bare (e.g. "10.5066/F7J1015K"), not a full URL.

sci:citation.description: STAC Scientific Citation extension. Full formatted citation text for this dataset itself (author, year, title, publisher, etc.). May contain Markdown.

sci:publications.description: STAC Scientific Citation extension. Other publications that used this dataset -- distinct from sci:citation/sci:doi, which are the dataset's own citation.

href.description: Same href convention as an item's asset href below -- our own bucket, a foreign s3:// bucket (falls back to default_endpoint), or a bare https:// URL.

assets.description: STAC Collection-level assets -- a map keyed by asset key, e.g. `thumbnail` (replaces schema_version 1's dedicated `overview_image` field with the real STAC convention for exactly this: `assets: {thumbnail: {href, type, roles: ["thumbnail"]}}`).

items.description: Hand-authored list of individual data items (schema_version 1's `assets`). Exactly one of items/items_dir/stac_item/external_source/ept_source must be given -- see this schema's root-level oneOf.

items_dir.description: Alternative to items for a large batch of files we already hold in our own bucket (schema_version 1's `assets_dir`; see its href pattern below -- this is only supported for our own bucket, not a foreign one). Exactly one of items/items_dir/stac_item/external_source/ept_source must be given.

stac_item.description: Alternative to items/items_dir: a pointer to a contributor's own already-complete STAC Item document (geometry, bbox, pc:*/proj:* properties, assets already filled in) -- lets a contributor who already has one skip retyping that same information into items[] by hand. Ingest fetches it at ingest time and reads its assets/geometry/properties directly; our own container pipeline still processes the real asset bytes for hero-image/derivative/elevation-stats generation regardless, exactly as it would for a hand-authored items[] entry -- this only saves re-describing data that's already described somewhere real. Exactly one of items/items_dir/stac_item/external_source/ept_source must be given.

external_source.description: Alternative to items/items_dir/stac_item/ept_source: a pointer into someone else's already-cataloged STAC document, when its Items/child-Collections should each become their own pointcloud.org dataset (see `expand`) rather than describing a single dataset. Exactly one of items/items_dir/stac_item/external_source/ept_source must be given.

ept_source.description: Alternative to items/items_dir/stac_item/external_source: a single Entwine Point Tile (EPT) resource, read directly via PDAL's readers.ept and displayed in-browser via Eptium's native EPT support -- never copied into our own bucket (no `federate` support) and never converted to COPC, since it's a multi-file hierarchy (ept.json + ept-data/ + ept-hierarchy/) rather than one downloadable file. Exactly one of items/items_dir/stac_item/external_source/ept_source must be given.

name.description: The organization itself, e.g. "USGS" or "Civil Engineering and Development Department (CEDD), HKSARG" -- flat, matching STAC's own provider object (schema_version 1 nested this under organization.name).

contact.description: The person who can actually update this dataset's manifest/URLs on this organization's behalf, if any -- gets emailed if ingest preflight fails. No STAC equivalent, hence nested under pointcloud_org rather than a plain provider field.

derivatives.description: Generate DTM/DSM/ambient-occlusion COGs at ingest time? Purely a pointcloud.org processing instruction -- no STAC equivalent.

federate.description: Optional, default false. When true, ingest copies every item's bytes from wherever this manifest currently points (a foreign bucket or a bare https:// URL) into pointcloud.org's own storage once, at ingest time, then treats that copy as authoritative for all further processing instead of re-fetching from the original source. Meaningful only for a hand-authored `items` list or a `stac_item` reference (items_dir is already restricted to our own bucket; external_source points at someone else's whole STAC catalog, not individual items) -- ignored otherwise. Use this when a dataset's original host is not reliably durable (a personal server, a time-limited hosting arrangement) and the intent is to actually archive a copy here, not just link out to it.

default_endpoint.description: Fallback S3 API endpoint for every item asset href in this manifest that doesn't set its own `endpoint` -- see README.md's "Endpoints" section.

derivative_processing.description: Optional; only consulted when pointcloud_org.derivatives is true. Every field falls back to the engine's default when omitted.

id.description: An explicit horizontal spatial reference identifier for this dataset, e.g. "EPSG:26912". Only set this when the source metadata states one explicitly -- don't infer/guess it from the data itself.

spatial_reference.description: Purely informational -- doesn't feed any ingest-time CRS handling (that comes from the data itself / items_dir's CRS-consistency preflight check).

acknowledgement.description: Funding/acknowledgement text a data provider asks to be included whenever the dataset is used. No STAC equivalent.

publication_date.description: ISO 8601 date or timestamp. When this dataset was published/released, as distinct from extent.temporal (when the data was acquired). No standardized STAC Collection field for this.

href.description: An absolute https:// URL, OR a path relative to this manifest's own directory pointing at a file checked into the repo alongside manifest.yaml. Relative paths are resolved by the site build, never by the ingest backend.

metadata_links.description: Pointers to externally-hosted or locally-checked-in metadata about this dataset (flight reports, sensor/acquisition documentation, FGDC/ISO XML, etc.). Purely informational -- never processed by any ingest stage. Distinct from top-level `links`/STAC Link objects because of the relative-path resolution behavior above, which generic STAC links don't define.

href.description: "s3://pointcloud/..." (our own bucket), "s3://<other-bucket>/..." (foreign bucket, resolved via endpoint/default_endpoint), a bare https:// URL, or a GDAL VSI path (/vsicurl/, /vsis3/, etc.).

endpoint.description: S3 API endpoint for this asset's href -- falls back to pointcloud_org.default_endpoint if omitted. See README.md's "Endpoints" section.

data.description: Matches the shape of a real generated STAC Item's own `assets.data` entry exactly (schema_version 1 kept href/roles/endpoint directly on the item, not nested under assets.data).

copc_resolution.description: The finest COPC hierarchy resolution to expose for this item (schema_version 1's `copc.resolution`). An ingest-time processing hint, not an intrinsic STAC property, hence nested here.

href.description: Only supported for our own bucket -- must be an "s3://pointcloud/..." prefix, since this is listed directly by pointcloud.org's own infrastructure.

pattern.description: Single leading "*" wildcard (suffix match), not a full glob. Defaults to "*.copc.laz".

href.description: URL to a complete external STAC Item JSON document (geometry, bbox, assets, and ideally the pointcloud/projection extensions' pc:*/proj:* properties already populated).

copc_resolution.description: Optional override/hint for the COPC hierarchy resolution to expose. When omitted, ingest attempts to infer a reasonable value from the referenced Item's own pc:schemas/spacing information, falling back to the engine's default.

href.description: URL to a STAC ItemCollection, Catalog, or Collection JSON document.

expand.description: true: href's Items/child-Collections each become their own pointcloud.org dataset (dry-run only as of 2026-08-01, see externalCatalog.ts). false/omitted: href itself is a single Collection to mirror as this one dataset.

href.description: URL to an Entwine Point Tile (EPT) resource's root document -- must end in "ept.json", the exact suffix both PDAL's readers.ept auto-detection and Eptium's own in-browser viewer key off of.

ept_catalog_id.description: The id this resource is cataloged under in USGS's own EPT STAC catalog (https://usgs-lidar-stac.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ept/catalog.json), if any. Also used at ingest time as the join key into USGS's WESM (Workunit Extent Spatial Metadata) CSV -- when set, it's looked up there to populate the generated STAC Item's start_datetime/end_datetime, since an EPT resource's own root ept.json document has no acquisition-date field of its own. Leave unset to skip that lookup (the Item's datetime, start_datetime, and end_datetime will all be left unset).

copc_resolution.description: Optional override/hint for the point-cloud octree resolution to expose in the generated STAC Item and Eptium viewer -- same name as stac_item's own override despite referring to an EPT resource, since EPT and COPC share the same octree-resolution concept.

resolution.description: GSD in meters for all derivative rasters. Falls back to each item's pointcloud_org.copc_resolution when omitted.

pdal_filters.description: Inline filter stages. Mutually exclusive with pdal_filters_file. Replaces the engine's default pipeline entirely when given -- no 'append to defaults' mode.

pdal_filters_file.description: Path, relative to this manifest's own directory, to a JSON file containing just the filter-stages array. Mutually exclusive with pdal_filters. Resolved (read + parsed + inlined as pdal_filters) by build-datasets-payload.mjs before the manifest ever reaches the ingest backend.

pdalFilterStage.description: {"type": "filters.range", ...} etc, as PDAL itself expects. Not validated further -- passed through to the Container verbatim.
